votes.refutation: I checked rate-limit handling, task-failure telemetry, and the existing restart tests. Rate limits already honor retry_after with a minimum sixty-second wait (:1160-1162), so the simple five-second rate-limit premise is too broad. Task failures and retries already have counters (posthog/celery.py:265-274), refuting the suggestion that no failure metric exists. test_tasks.py:974-1001 covers restarting queued or failed runs on a later output refire, but does not reconcile a trigger exhausted before it creates any row. A config-DB outage causing prompt errors can still consume the three five-second retries, and subsequent status-only saves are ignored by the receiver. Later output updates/pushes provide a workaround, so the real missed-review gap is should_fix rather than must_fix.
